pr_title: Use the type RefName for all the needed places and fix pull mirror sync bugs
pr_body:
This PR replaces all string refName as a type `git.RefName` to make the code more maintainable.

Fix #15367
Replaces #23070 
It also fixed a bug that tags are not sync because `git remote --prune origin` will not remove local tags if remote removed.

We in fact should use `git fetch --prune --tags origin` but not `git remote update origin` to do the sync.

Some answer from ChatGPT as ref.

> If the git fetch --prune --tags command is not working as expected, there could be a few reasons why. Here are a few things to check:
> 
>Make sure that you have the latest version of Git installed on your system. You can check the version by running git --version in your terminal. If you have an outdated version, try updating Git and see if that resolves the issue.
> 
>Check that your Git repository is properly configured to track the remote repository's tags. You can check this by running git config --get-all remote.origin.fetch and verifying that it includes +refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*. If it does not, you can add it by running git config --add remote.origin.fetch "+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*".
> 
>Verify that the tags you are trying to prune actually exist on the remote repository. You can do this by running git ls-remote --tags origin to list all the tags on the remote repository.
> 
>Check if any local tags have been created that match the names of tags on the remote repository. If so, these local tags may be preventing the git fetch --prune --tags command from working properly. You can delete local tags using the git tag -d command.
pr_comments: I think the design of "ShortName()" is not ideal, it would cause more abuses, because it's unclear about what the name it is. It could be a tag, or it could be a branch, but callers would keep forgetting to check whether it is a branch or it is a tag.

> I think the design of "ShortName()" is not ideal, it would cause more abuses, because it's unclear about what the name it is. It could be a tag, or it could be a branch, but callers would keep forgetting to check whether it is a branch or it is a tag.

The code `opts.RefFullName.ShortName() == repo.DefaultBranch` is worse than before (full ref compare). Sooner or later there will be more abuses.

According to #25185 , some field values are changed from "tag" to "tags", it breaks some APIs and 3rdparty systems.
"ref_type" also affects "branch" -> "heads" , which seems also breaking.

I tired resetting the default branch but it doesn't work.

Also I didn't see any error in the logs. I am sure that I have RepoIndexerEnabled, as the code search works for plain repos instead of the mirrored ones.

review_comments: @a1012112796 Maybe you can give some suggestions about this condition?

I guess you created more conflicts with your "notification refactoring" PR.

Keeping doing so, some code would be lost sooner or later.

Could these PRs not be stale for that long? I would propose to discard that stale PR.
The change is not too big to handle.

I guess here (and above) it needs to check `IsBranch` or `IsTag` first?

Otherwise, if the pattern is `*`, then a branch's TagName returns `""`, it matches the pattern `*` ?

(Maybe a legacy problem)
This has been checked, see line 236
When reading this line, I guess `AgitBranchName` is clearer 🤣
The `refs/for/xx` is used by Gerrit first as a 3rd usage and then merged into git. So for now, both gerrit and agit will use it.

1. The test function name should be updated?
2. Should the `for` (and more) be tested?
We currently don't support that. The branch name in `For()` is the target branch name not the head branch name. For `For`, there is no head branch concept.

```suggestion
	if setting.Indexer.RepoIndexerEnabled && opts.RefFullName.EqualBranchName(repo.DefaultBranch) {
```

Like this? Simpler than before and couldn't be misused.
But sometimes, we need to send branch name as parameter but not compare the branch name. If we do that, we will have both `Branchname()` and `EqualBranchName()` and `IsBranch` still need to be kept.
Curious, `fetch` works better than old `remote update`?
Yes, it's recommended to use `fetch`, I will add a comment here.
